why: A moves the same five sites with the same safety model but delivers materially deeper system judgment: a complete call inventory (it alone found the chart tool's Node subprocess LLM call), two-vendor cache measurements that corrected the no-key-no-caching assumption, the discovery that [llm.<agent>] config is dead code behind an unreachable validator branch, measured auto-router and cheap-first-with-escalation proposals including the output-cap trap, provider_timeout for a loop whose SDK timeout is 300s, and the enumerated defects in the Bedrock shim — plus it actually built the retry fix with the coupled ToolCallAgent.think unwrapping that B only identifies as necessary. B is tighter and safer in scope and lands one catch A missed outright (always-image/jpeg base64 labels, which 400 on Anthropic), but leaves the biggest levers unexplored and ships one claim that A's own live data contradicts.
A_best: Depth on this specific app: the dead per-agent config discovery, the switchyard measurement ($0.000109 vs $0.003184 with honest n=4 and quality caveats), cheap-first escalation reusing the existing is_stuck detector with the 300-token truncation trap shown, and the enumerated Bedrock-shim defects (module-global CURRENT_TOOLUSE_ID, lost system messages) — judgment that reads the product, not just the catalog.
B_best: Finding that format_messages hardcodes image/jpeg on every base64 image, proving it live (6x400 from Anthropic on a PNG), and recognising that widening the multimodal list without that fix converts silent image loss into a hard failure — the one place B's built work is more correct than A's.
A_worst: Its per-agent-llm branch fails the parse gate with a SyntaxError in data_visualization.py, and its catalog-driven image widening ships without B's media-type fix, so browser screenshots (the base64_image path) would newly 400 on exactly the Claude models it unblocks.
B_worst: Shallower system review: no consideration of auto-routing or provider_timeout, the obviously-correct retry fix left unbuilt, the chart tool's LLM call missing from the inventory entirely, "loses: nothing" on the move itself, and the claim that the cache-key policy is a no-op on Claude, which A's measurement (cached 0 both calls without a key) refutes.
